key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast perovskite photoluminescence degradation from stressed time-series data, enabling long-term stability prediction on unseen samples.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster, explainable screening tool for perovskite stability, potentially reducing the need for prolonged accelerated ageing experiments.
method: Collected 167 metal halide perovskite samples with varied compositions and crystallinity.
Stressed samples with heat and light while recording more than 86,000 photoluminescence spectra.
Featurized spectra with a physics-informed model and trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity.
evidence_signal: The model generalized across material groups and outperformed baseline benchmarks when forecasting degradation of samples not seen during training.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of the training dataset, especially for new perovskite chemistries or measurement conditions.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
